correctness.rationale: The cube has edge connectivity d, so the deletion leaves a positive definite Laplacian on the zero-mean space. The Woodbury trace correction for incidence columns B is N times the trace of (I−BᵀL⁺B)⁻¹ Bᵀ(L⁺)²B, yielding the stated fraction with c>|t|. In the Walsh expansion an incidence column is supported on characters containing its direction. For parallel pairs the signed summands from the j differing base coordinates expand (1−z)^j; for perpendicular pairs the two forced directions contribute one extra z after integration. Both mixed correlations have the same sign and their absolute values strictly decrease with j. Thus it suffices to compare incident edges and opposite parallel edges in a square. For k=0,1 the ratios of the z-weighted to the (1−z)-weighted integrals under the common density proportional to (−log z)^k(1+z)^(d−2) strictly increase with d, since tilting by 1+z increases E[z] by Var(z)/(1+E[z]). The first ratio exceeds one at d=3. The product of the ratios exceeds one at d=5 by the binomial integrals (t_T u_T−t_P u_P=241/491520) and thereafter. Hence for d≥5 both numerator and reciprocal denominator strictly favor incident edges; only c,s>0 is needed for the monotonicity, not the stronger c>s in the text. For d=3,4 an independent grounded inverse, summing electrical resistances, gave incident versus closest parallel values 154/5 versus 214/7, and 4004/51 versus 36296/465, respectively. The resulting gaps 8/35 and 1196/2635 equal the frozen per-vertex gaps multiplied by 2^d. The equality class and 2^d binom(d,2) count follow by strict comparison and the unique shared vertex. The intact trace baseline follows from eigenvalues 2k with multiplicities binom(d,k).
residual_risks: The grounded calculation checks the two exceptional dimensions, not the general classification. The latter rests on the strict integral comparisons and connected rank-two identity.
